- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and forecast is above recent mean, apply downward bias of 3–7% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent peak), reduce forecast by 10–15% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 5+ days, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence to recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.25+), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If true outcome is below 65% of 30-day forecast mean, assume model is overconfident — apply downward adjustment of 5–10% for next 7 days.
